prompt: `build_iret_frame` returns `frame`, the lowest of the five slots that `iretq` pops. Fill in each slot for a ring 3 program with interrupts disabled.
code:
uint64_t *frame = build_iret_frame(top, entry, user_sp);
__asm__ volatile("mov %0, %%rsp; iretq" :: "r"(frame));
explain: `iretq` pops rip, cs, rflags, rsp and ss, lowest address first. The user code selector 0x23 has RPL 3, so the CPU enters ring 3 and therefore also loads rsp and ss (0x1B, user data). RFLAGS 0x2 has only the always-one reserved bit set, so IF is clear.
